title: StronglyConvexDueling.lean

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: The strong-convexity inequality with μ > 0 implies convexity on the ball.

problem_class.label: strongly_convex
problem_class.details: The objective is continuously differentiable on ℝᵈ. On the closed unit ball it is μ-strongly convex and G-Lipschitz, and its gradient is L-Lipschitz. The minimizer is taken over the ball and may lie on its boundary.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StronglyConvexDueling.lean, Objective.differentiable, Objective.continuous_gradient, Objective.strongly_convex, Objective.lipschitz, Objective.smooth and spec.successful

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: Each call compares two feasible points x and y and returns one bit. Conditional on the query and past observations, the probability of true is (1 + ρ(f(x) − f(y)))/2. Each call uses a fresh independent seed with the same law. The algorithm receives the comparison bit alone.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StronglyConvexDueling.lean, score, spec.Query, spec.Reply and spec.admissible. LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean, IID

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: Queries and output lie in the closed Euclidean unit ball of ℝᵈ, with public integer d ≥ 1.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StronglyConvexDueling.lean, Point, Ball, Params.nonzero, spec.Query, spec.Output and spec.publicInput

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The hidden transfer function ρ is odd, nondecreasing, continuously differentiable and bounded by 1 in absolute value. For |t| ≤ r it satisfies c|t|ᵏ ≤ ρ′(t) ≤ M. Thus k = 0 gives a positive local slope floor, while k > 0 allows the slope to vanish at a tie. The algorithm knows d, k and the positive parameters μ, L, G, r, c, M and ε. The objective and transfer function are hidden.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StronglyConvexDueling.lean, Params, Transfer, spec.Public, spec.publicInput, spec.valid and spec.admissible

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The algorithm returns a measurable feasible point X. For a minimizer u over the closed unit ball, the objective gap f(X) − f(u) must be integrable.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The required bound is E[f(X) − f(u)] ≤ ε under the joint law of the algorithm and oracle seeds, with a fixed upper bound on the number of comparison calls.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The learner observes only binary comparisons through an unknown transfer function. Its local derivative bound specifies how weak the comparison signal may become near equal objective values.

descriptionHtml:
Strongly Convex Minimization with Comparisons

We minimize a continuously differentiable function f:Rd→R over the closed Euclidean unit ball B in dimension d≥1. On B, f is strongly convex and Lipschitz with Lipschitz gradient. For each query x,y∈B, the oracle uses a fresh independent sample to return a sign in {−1,1} with mean ρ(f(x)−f(y)), where ρ is an unknown odd, nondecreasing function with local derivative bounds. Given ε>0, the goal is a feasible output x¯∈B with E[f(x¯)−f(x⋆)]≤ε, where x⋆ minimizes f on B and the expectation includes algorithm and oracle randomness.

With ∥⋅∥ denoting the Euclidean norm, the constrained problem is minx∈Bf(x),B={x∈Rd:∥x∥≤1}. The algorithm receives the dimension d, the objective constants μ,L,G>0, the transfer parameters r,c,M>0 and k∈{0,1,2,…}, and the tolerance ε.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Objective regularity and strong convexity). The function f is continuously differentiable on Rd. For every x,y∈B, it satisfies |f(y)−f(x)|≤G∥y−x∥,∥∇f(y)−∇f(x)∥≤L∥y−x∥,f(y)−f(x)≥⟨∇f(x),y−x⟩+μ2∥y−x∥2.

Assumption 2 (Comparison transfer). The transfer function ρ:R→[−1,1] is continuously differentiable, odd, and nondecreasing. Its derivative satisfies c|t|k≤ρ′(t)≤M,|t|≤r, where |t|0=1 for every t.

Assumption 3 (Pairwise comparison oracle). Let Z1,Z2,… be independent random variables with common law ν on a measurable space Z, independent of the algorithm’s randomness. On call j with ordered pair (x,y)∈B×B, the oracle returns the bit g(x,y,Zj) encoded as a sign, where g:B×B×Z→{−1,1} is jointly measurable. For every x,y∈B, EZ∼ν[g(x,y,Z)]=ρ(f(x)−f(y)).

After the allotted comparisons, the output x¯ must be a measurable B-valued random variable. For a minimizer x⋆∈B, the gap f(x¯)−f(x⋆) must be integrable under the joint law of the algorithm’s randomness and the oracle samples and satisfy E[f(x¯)−f(x⋆)]≤ε.

comparisonHtml:
On the closed Euclidean unit ball B⊂Rd, f∈C1(Rd) is μ-strongly convex, L-smooth and G-Lipschitz. Each pair x,y∈B yields one sign from a jointly measurable oracle with fresh IID noise and mean ρ(f(x)−f(y)). The unknown odd, nondecreasing C1 link satisfies |ρ|≤1 and c|t|k≤ρ′(t)≤M for |t|≤r. The parameters are public, with d≥1, integer k≥0 and μ,L,G,r,c,M,ε>0. The target is E[f(x^)−minBf]≤ε for a measurable x^∈B.

Sufficient comparison budgets for strongly convex optimization with dueling feedback.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) LocalReferenceDueling (Ours) (⋆⋆⋆) (review) O(1+d2C2s2με+d2M2L2s4μ2ε2)
(2) Epoch-PDD (Saha et al. 2025, Thm. 4) Derived bound on B for expected gap, using tolerance ε/2 and δ=ε/(4G): O(K+dc2(aLdμε)2k+2log⁡(eK/δ)). Here 0<δ<1 and ε/2<5Lmin{4d,2dr/G}. (1): For fixed k≥1 and sufficiently small ε with other parameters fixed, fixed-distance opponents reduce d2k+3/ε2k+2 to d2/ε2 (at k=1, d5/ε4 before logs). At k=0, the leading polynomial cost improves for d≫(M/c)2. All queries stay feasible, even for constrained boundary minima. (1): Weighted-average expectation only. (2) gives a high-probability final epoch point on general bounded domains containing a global minimizer, with exterior queries allowed. (1) needs an odd C1 link and M; its accuracy term carries C8kμ−(4k+2) versus μ−(2k+2).
(3) NC-SMD (Kumagai 2017, Thms. 4, 13) Derived bound on B with full-range slope bounds (k=0): O((A+H)log⁡(e+A+H) +AH+GM0/(mε)). (1): Removes the accuracy logarithm at fixed parameters. Allows C1 objectives and locally controlled flat links. For ρ=tanh, r=1 and maxBf−minBf≍G, dependence on large G is polynomial versus exponential. (1): The ε−2 coefficient can be larger for small G and large ML/(cμ). (3) also bounds online regret on compact convex domains with a barrier, assuming C2 objectives and a thrice differentiable link with positive, nonincreasing slope on the positive gap range.
(4) Coordinate descent (Jamieson et al. 2012, Thm. 2) O(d2k+3ε−2(k+1) polylog(d,1/ε,1/δ)) for fixed class and oracle parameters, margin exponent κ=k+2, confidence 1−δ. (1): Covers constrained minima with in-ball comparisons. Rates are not directly comparable: (4) assumes unconstrained optimization on Rd. (1) needs a fixed link. (4) requires only a lower margin on the probability of a correct comparison.

Abbr: C=max{1,8G/r}, s=c(μ/(4C2))k, K=1+max{0,⌈log2⁡(4L/ε)⌉}, and a>0 is a universal constant. Over the attained gap range, m≤ρ′≤M0 and |ρ″|≤B2 in (3). A=d2/(mε)2 and H=1+[B2G2+(G+1)M0L]/(mμ).

import LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.PiL2
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Lp.MeasurableSpace

open MeasureTheory
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.StronglyConvexDueling

open OracleTemplate

abbrev Point (d : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)
abbrev Ball (d : ℕ) := Metric.closedBall (0 : Point d) 1

structure Params where
  d : ℕ
  [nonzero : NeZero d]
  μ : ℝ
  L : ℝ
  G : ℝ
  r : ℝ
  c : ℝ
  M : ℝ
  k : ℕ
  ε : ℝ

attribute [instance] Params.nonzero

structure Objective (p : Params) (f : Point p.d → ℝ) : Prop where
  differentiable : ∀ x, HasGradientAt f (gradient f x) x
  continuous_gradient : Continuous (gradient f)
  lipschitz : ∀ x ∈ Ball p.d, ∀ y ∈ Ball p.d, |f x - f y| ≤ p.G * ‖x - y‖
  smooth : ∀ x ∈ Ball p.d, ∀ y ∈ Ball p.d,
    ‖gradient f x - gradient f y‖ ≤ p.L * ‖x - y‖
  strongly_convex : ∀ x ∈ Ball p.d, ∀ y ∈ Ball p.d,
    f x + ⟪gradient f x, y - x⟫ + p.μ / 2 * ‖y - x‖ ^ 2 ≤ f y

structure Transfer (p : Params) (ρ : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop where
  differentiable : ∀ t, HasDerivAt ρ (deriv ρ t) t
  continuous_derivative : Continuous (deriv ρ)
  odd : ∀ t, ρ (-t) = -ρ t
  monotone : Monotone ρ
  bounded : ∀ t, |ρ t| ≤ 1
  slope_lower : ∀ t, |t| ≤ p.r → p.c * |t| ^ p.k ≤ deriv ρ t
  slope_upper : ∀ t, |t| ≤ p.r → deriv ρ t ≤ p.M

def score (b : Bool) : ℝ := if b then 1 else -1

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := Point p.d → ℝ
  Query p := Ball p.d × Ball p.d
  Reply _ := Bool
  Output p := Ball p.d
  publicInput := id
  valid p := 0 < p.μ ∧ 0 < p.L ∧ 0 < p.G ∧ 0 < p.r ∧ 0 < p.c ∧ 0 < p.M ∧ 0 < p.ε
  admissible p f O := Objective p f ∧ ∃ ρ, Transfer p ρ ∧
    ∃ (Ω : Type) (_ : MeasurableSpace Ω) (ν : ProbabilityMeasure Ω)
      (P : ProbabilityMeasure (ℕ → Ω)) (g : (Ball p.d × Ball p.d) → Ω → Bool),
      StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.IID (fun k (ω : ℕ → Ω) => ω k) ν P ∧
      Measurable (Function.uncurry g) ∧
      (∀ x, (∫ z, score (g x z) ∂(ν : Measure Ω)) = ρ (f x.1.val - f x.2.val)) ∧
      O = { Seed := fun _ => Ω, law := P, answer := fun _ (_, x) z => g x z }
  successful p f out P := Measurable out ∧ ∃ u : Ball p.d, IsMinOn f (Ball p.d) u.val ∧
    Integrable (fun ω => f (out ω).val - f u.val) (P : Measure _) ∧
    (∫ ω, f (out ω).val - f u.val ∂(P : Measure _)) ≤ p.ε

end LongTails.Setups.StronglyConvexDueling
